name: Lush
label: 4AD
lede: Two school friends who couldn't play when they started got a 4AD deal, a Cocteau Twin producing, a Lollapalooza slot and a Britpop top ten, then lost their drummer a month after their last show.

eras.title: From a fanzine to a 4AD sleeve
eras.text: Miki Berenyi and Emma Anderson met at 14 at Queen's College in London and wrote a fanzine before either could play. By the end of 1989 they had a record out on the label that put out the Cocteau Twins.

years.cap: Miki Berenyi and Emma Anderson at a My Bloody Valentine show, London
years.h: The Baby Machines form around a North London Poly drummer
years.p: [[Miki Berenyi|00f7467f-462e-408c-8d57-ac10f33d8139]] meets drummer Chris Acland and singer Meriel Barham at North London Polytechnic. With her school friend [[Emma Anderson|e081e59f-78b8-4f16-8f7b-de06ee155d8f]] and bassist Steve Rippon, they become the Baby Machines.
years.xp:
Berenyi and Anderson had met at 14 at Queen's College, a private school in London, and put out five issues of a music fanzine called Alphabet Soup. In 1986 Anderson played in Rover Girls and Berenyi played bass in the Bugs.

The name came from a line in [[Siouxsie and the Banshees|78ea5ea1-3c4d-4b7e-ac5d-68900319ebe2]]' 'Arabian Knights'. It didn't last: by the first gig they were Lush.

years.src: Light from a Dead Star: Gigography · Wikipedia: Lush
yt: Live at the Fulham Greyhound, April 6, 1988
years.h: Lush plays its first gig at the Camden Falcon
years.p: Five-piece Lush, with Meriel Barham singing, opens a bill with the Rosehips at the Camden pub that hosted half of London's guitar bands.

years.src: Light from a Dead Star: Miki's
years.h: A Play School presenter sits in on saxophone
years.p: At Ealing College the band is joined by Fred Harris, familiar to every British child of the 1970s from the BBC's Play School.

years.h: Meriel Barham leaves for Pale Saints; Berenyi takes the mic
years.p: Barham goes on to sing in [[Pale Saints|1584532a-62ed-4cbe-ad95-6def0af7df35]]. Berenyi moves to lead vocals and stays there.
years.xp: Anderson's summary of the early plan: "extremely loud guitars with much weaker vocals." Berenyi said the first songs were "crappy riot grrrl anthems" until Anderson brought in 'Thoughtforms' and the writing got more thoughtful.

years.src: Light from a Dead Star: Miki's
years.h: My Bloody Valentine's drummer saves a Camden Falcon show
years.p: The Sun Carriage's drummer won't share his kit, so Colm Ó Cíosóig of [[My Bloody Valentine|8ca01f46-53ac-4af2-8516-55a909c0905e]] sorts out drums at the last minute.

q: Now we've got a record out on 4AD.
years.h: Scar, six songs on 4AD
years.p: 4AD signs the band in 1989, and the mini-album gets it the first wave of press. The papers soon file Lush under a new word: shoegaze.
years.xp: Anderson told Melody Maker she remembered not being able to play and not being in a band, and found it "impossible to come to terms with what's happening."

years.src: Light from a Dead Star: Miki's
years.h: A Glasgow power cut stops the set, and the review is bad anyway
years.p: At Glasgow's QMC the power fails before Lush can play; only Loop gets on. A review still says Scotland should close its borders to Lush.

eras.title: A Cocteau Twin at the desk
eras.text: Two EPs with outside producers put Lush in the UK singles chart and on US alternative radio. Then came Glastonbury, Japan and a first American tour with Ride.

years.h: Robin Guthrie produces the Mad Love EP
years.p: The [[Cocteau Twins|000fc734-b7e1-4a01-92d1-f544261b43f5]] guitarist takes the desk, and the EP reaches No. 55 in the UK.

years.cap: Lush and Pale Saints on stage together at L'Ubu, Rennes, March 1990
years.src: Light from a Dead Star: Gigography · Wikipedia: Lush
years.h: Glastonbury, on a bill with Pale Saints
years.p: Lush plays Pilton alongside Barham's new band. The band records a John Peel session for BBC Radio 1 the same year.

years.h: Lush covers 'Chirpy Chirpy Cheep Cheep' against the poll tax
years.p: The band's version of the Middle of the Road bubblegum hit goes on Alvin Lives (In Leeds), a benefit album against Thatcher's poll tax.

years.h: Sweetness and Light goes to No. 4 on US alternative radio
years.p: Tim Friese-Greene produces. The EP reaches No. 47 in the UK and No. 4 on the US alternative chart.

years.cap: Lush live at SUNY Purchase, New York, March 21, 1991
years.src: Light from a Dead Star: Gigography · Wikipedia: Lush
years.h: Lush and Ride cross North America together
years.p: Five weeks of shows with [[Ride|3f575ecd-627d-4f08-a89f-abd46d469c7e]], March 20 to April 24. The tour does as much as the records to build Lush an American audience.

years.src: Wikipedia: Chris Acland · Wikipedia: Miki Berenyi
years.h: Acland records a flexi for Tottenham's win over Arsenal
years.p: Spurs fan Chris Acland celebrates the 1991 FA Cup semi-final with a joke flexi-disc, 'And David Seaman Will Be Very Disappointed About That'.
years.xp: The same year Acland and Berenyi joined members of [[Cocteau Twins|000fc734-b7e1-4a01-92d1-f544261b43f5]] and [[Moose|0ecd90fd-5eac-40ad-bcec-31ca34fe6318]] as the Lillies, who released one song.

years.h: 'For Love' gives Lush its first UK top 40
years.p: The single reaches No. 35. The B-sides include 'Astronaut', the only Lush song with Anderson on lead vocal, and a cover of [[Wire|7f2a8098-50e3-451c-8696-c5d9f64f4762]]'s 'Outdoor Miner'.

eras.title: Top ten, nine weeks on the road, a record mixed three times
eras.text: Spooky went top ten in Britain and Perry Farrell put Lush on Lollapalooza. The follow-up took a producer, two mixing studios and a rescue remix to finish.

years.h: Spooky reaches No. 7 in the UK
years.p: Robin Guthrie produces the whole debut album and buries the band in his walls of guitar. It sells well; reviews are mixed.
years.xp: Critics' main complaint was that Guthrie's sound pulled the record away from what the band had set out to do. It still became Lush's first top-ten album.

years.cap: Lush with Phil King at the Luxor, Cologne, May 12, 1992
years.h: Steve Rippon quits to write a novel; Phil King joins
years.p: Rippon leaves after the 'For Love' sessions to concentrate on writing. His book, Cold Turkey Sandwich, is turned down by publishers. [[Felt|6999f790-25f4-44a3-b745-1e3e01fde0f5]] veteran Phil King takes the bass.

years.cap: Chris Acland, Phil King, Miki Berenyi and Emma Anderson backstage at Lollapalooza, c. 1992
years.src: Wikipedia: Lush · Light from a Dead Star: Gigography · Light from a Dead Star: Phil's · Light from a Dead Star: Miki's
years.h: Perry Farrell puts Lush on Lollapalooza
years.p: Farrell asks for the band himself. From Mountain View on July 18 to Irvine on September 13, Lush opens a bill with [[Red Hot Chili Peppers|8bfac288-ccc5-448d-9573-c33ea2aa5c30]], [[Ministry|13df2a46-f72f-40e7-aa63-26fcf62c7048]], [[Soundgarden|153c9281-268f-4cf3-8938-f5a4593e5df4]] and [[Pearl Jam|83b9cbe7-9857-49e2-ab8e-b57b01038103]].
years.xp:
Phil King kept a tour diary. In Dallas, Berenyi stage-dived into an empty seated section and needed hospital treatment and stitches. By the last Los Angeles dates everybody was jamming with everybody; King called it "a deranged version of Live Aid."

Berenyi admits she brought Ulysses and language tapes and gave up on self-improvement after three days. Touring, she wrote, is "a mobile prison, but in a fun way."

years.big: £500 in coins, spent on the producer's pinball machine
q: I wanted to hang from his shoulders weeping with gratitude.
years.src: Light from a Dead Star: Miki's · Wikipedia: Lush
years.h: Mike Hedges records Split; nobody likes the mix
years.p: Two mixes, at Abbey Road and at Hedges's studio in Domfront, France, satisfy neither the band nor Watts-Russell. Alan Moulder is brought in to remix.
years.xp:
Berenyi remembers Domfront as the middle of nowhere, with nothing to do except a pinball machine the producer charged them to play. The band fed it about £500.

Meanwhile, she wrote, the manager had gone AWOL, their Warners A&R man was having a midlife crisis and Ivo had decided to retire. A meeting with Moulder and Scott Litt went the American's way; Litt's session didn't work, and Moulder finished the job.

years.h: Split lands at No. 19
years.p: The second album reaches No. 19 in the UK. Two EPs from it, 'Hypocrite' and 'Desire Lines', came out together on May 30 and stalled at No. 52 and No. 63.

years.h: A third EP is shelved and Lush changes managers
years.p: A planned autumn single is pulled, tours of Japan and the UK are cancelled, and the band leaves manager Howard Gough.

eras.title: Britpop, then the end
eras.text: Lovelife was the band's biggest record and its brightest. A tired American tour followed, Anderson talked about leaving, and in October 1996 Chris Acland died.

years.h: 'Single Girl' hits No. 21, with a video full of Four Weddings actors
years.p: Producer Pete Bartlett, the band's live engineer, heard a single straight away. Anderson kept calling it a B-side.
years.xp: Berenyi on Bartlett: "You and Emma seemed almost embarrassed by the idea of commercial success."

years.h: 'Ladykillers' borrows from the Monkees and nods at Courtney Love
years.p: The single reaches No. 22. In 2017 Berenyi said the song referenced [[Hole|1dcc8968-f2cd-441c-beda-6270f70f2863]]'s Courtney Love, but wasn't meant as a dig at her.
years.xp: Berenyi said the riff came from The Monkees and [[The Kinks|17b53d9f-5c63-4a09-a593-dde4608e0db9]]. 'Ladykillers' also made No. 18 on the US alternative chart.

years.cap: Lush live at the Electric Ballroom, Camden, April 3, 1996
years.h: Lovelife goes top ten, with Jarvis Cocker on 'Ciao!'
years.p: The band's best-selling album reaches No. 8. Berenyi wrote 'Ciao!' as a duet for Acland, who backed out; [[Pulp|76b2e842-5e85-4c97-ab62-d5bc315595b5]]'s [[Jarvis Cocker|38550441-d437-4aff-867e-e79bf0c04142]] sang it instead.
years.xp: Lighter on effects and closer to Britpop, Lovelife was made at Protocol in London and mastered by Bob Ludwig. Pitchfork later put it at No. 19 on its list of the 50 best Britpop albums.

years.h: Anderson passes her driving test and writes '500 (Shake Baby Shake)'
years.p: The song is about the Fiat 500. It reaches No. 21, the third top-30 single from Lovelife.

years.h: A US tour with Gin Blossoms wears the band down
years.p: Management sends Lush across America opening for Gin Blossoms. Anderson talks about leaving; she wants a smaller, more personal record, while Berenyi wants to keep going.

years.cap: Lush at the Liquid Room, Shinjuku, Tokyo, September 18, 1996
years.src: Light from a Dead Star: Gigography
years.h: Lush plays the Liquid Room in Tokyo, unaware it's the last show
years.p: The Shinjuku date closes a Japanese tour. It is the last time the original band plays together.

years.h: Chris Acland dies at 30
years.p: The drummer took his own life at his parents' home in Burneside, Cumbria. Wikipedia reports it came two days after Anderson said she intended to leave the band.

years.h: After sixteen months of silence, Lush announces the split
years.p: Berenyi goes to work as a magazine production editor. Anderson forms Sing-Sing with singer Lisa O'Neill. Phil King joins [[The Jesus and Mary Chain|e938a15c-b17e-4e7a-9f68-ff0d536cab44]] on bass.

eras.title: Elastica's drummer, a sold-out Roundhouse, one more goodbye
eras.text: Nineteen years after the last show, three of the four came back with Acland's old friend Justin Welch on drums. The reunion made new music, crossed America again and ended on purpose after a year.

years.cap: Emma Anderson, Miki Berenyi and Phil King in Lush's first reunion press photo, 2015
years.h: Lush reunites with Justin Welch of Elastica
years.p: A cryptic "7 day." post from Anderson and a new website get the press guessing; then it's official. Welch, of [[Elastica|46693641-1e2e-4aae-80ed-6b28170de63a]], was an old friend of Acland's.
years.xp:
The band's statement: "for many years, it was just too painful to contemplate without Chris."

4AD followed with Ciao! Best of Lush on red vinyl and Chorus, a five-CD box of rarities, sessions and demos. For Record Store Day 2016 came Origami, the albums on coloured vinyl in a white cardboard pizza box.

years.h: Blind Spot, the first new Lush songs in twenty years
years.p: Four tracks on Edamame Records, produced by Jim Abbiss and Ladytron's Daniel Hunt, including 'Burnham Beeches' and 'Lost Boy'.

years.cap: Lush on stage at the Roundhouse, London, May 6, 2016
years.src: Wikipedia: Lush · Light from a Dead Star: Gigography
years.h: The first Roundhouse night sells out in six hours
years.p: A second night is added for May 7. A warm-up at the Oslo in Hackney had sold out too, and the band's first North American tour in twenty years follows.

years.h: Modern English's Michael Conroy plays bass at the last Lush show
years.p: Phil King's exit is announced on October 18. With [[Modern English|78605d0c-7454-456d-934c-51eb46122566]]'s [[Michael Conroy|62391328-7b2e-49b9-8550-c606e5bb49f1]] on bass, Lush says goodbye at Manchester Academy.
years.xp: The farewell statement said it was "time for us to return to our families and homes."

eras.title: Piroshka, a memoir and two solo records
eras.text: The last Lush bass player and drummer stayed with Berenyi in a new band, and both songwriters made records of their own.

years.h: Berenyi, Welch and Conroy form Piroshka
years.p: With KJ "Moose" McKillop of [[Moose|0ecd90fd-5eac-40ad-bcec-31ca34fe6318]], Berenyi's partner. Brickbat comes out on Bella Union in February 2019 and Love Drips and Gathers in 2021.

years.h: Berenyi publishes Fingers Crossed
years.p: Subtitled How Music Saved Me from Success, the memoir tells her childhood and the band's story in her own words.

years.h: Both songwriters go solo
years.p: Anderson's Pearlies comes out on Sonic Cathedral in October 2023. In April 2025 the Miki Berenyi Trio, with McKillop and a drum machine, releases Tripla on Bella Union.
